messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: queue_length_high for service=redwood-runtime-prod region=us-west-2. threshold=120, current=312. Autoscaler lag detected. PagerDuty incident created: PD-4521

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-4521 triggered (high queue length). Assigned to on-call: @maria. Escalation policy: primary -> secondary -> sre-tl.

maria: acked PD-4521. jumping in. Thanks. Any current customer reports?

kevin: no direct customer tickets yet, but ingestion metrics show >90th percentile latency >2s for generation and token drop errors increasing.

sam: seeing node pressure on gpu-pool-3, pods in CrashLoopBackOff for the packer sidecar due to OOM. Might be memory leak in kvcache eviction.

jordan: I'm pulling k8s events now.

jordan: kubectl get pods -n runtime | grep gpu-pool-3
```
gpu-pod-3-7f8d   2/3   CrashLoopBackOff   5   5m
gpu-pod-3-9a1b   3/3   1/1     0   2m
...
```

dana: autoscaler logs show scale decisions delayed: "scale_decision_latency=45s, target_replicas=12, desired_replicas=24" around the time queue spiked.

maria: ok, high-level plan: 1) notify customer-impact (operations) 2) try manual surge to add nodes 3) mitigate by routing low-priority traffic to degraded model variant 4) investigate autoscaler control plane lag.

kevin: manual scale starting: increasing node pool gpu-pool-3 from 4 -> 12 nodes (request sent to cloud provider). ETA ~90s for node creation but warmup for runtime ~3-4m.

sam: creating a temporary routing rule to direct /embed requests to embed-async queue (lower priority) to reduce sync load. Pushing policy now.

maria: good. i'm posting a short customer-impact note for support: "We are experiencing increased request latency and a partial backlog in inference queues in us-west-2. Some requests may see degraded performance or delayed responses. Engineers are actively mitigating. Will update every 10 minutes."

pagerduty-bot: PD-4521 acknowledged by maria. ETA for first mitigation update: 10m.

jordan: attaching snippet from autoscaler controller logs around spike:
```
2026-03-14T14:02:01Z WARN scale_controller: evaluation_time=0.045s queue_len=298 desired=24 current=12
2026-03-14T14:02:02Z ERROR reconcile: failed to update nodegroup: rate limit exceeded (429)
2026-03-14T14:02:15Z INFO fallback: attempted to allocate spot nodes, insufficient capacity
```

dana: cloud provider returned ENI allocation delays; also hitting quota for GPUs in region temporarily.

kevin: manual capacity workaround: spinning up fallback cpu-backed nodes with fewer GPUs per instance to at least accept requests and drain queue. Starting nodegroup fallback-cpu-1.

sam: routing change applied. low-priority traffic reduced by ~35% within 30s. Queue growth rate plateaued.

maria: monitoring metrics... queue now 270 -> 210 after routing, so moving in right direction.

jordan: nodes coming up: 3/12 ready now. Runtime shards warming, but kv-cache miss rate is high while warming.

maria: stack traces show packer sidecar OOMs, config pin at 2Gi. Can we increase memory limit temporarily?

kevin: bumping sidecar memory to 4Gi for new pods; will roll new pods into gpu pool as nodes become ready.

sam: applied mem bump. Got a couple of successful restarts. CrashLoop count decreasing.

maria: good. customer-impact update: "We are serving most traffic but with degraded latency for some requests. Autoscaling delayed due to cloud capacity and quota errors; we have manually provisioned fallback capacity and reduced non-critical traffic. Root cause investigation underway." @support-team please escalate to affected accounts if needed.

pagerduty-bot: PD-4521 escalated to sre-tl after 12m without resolution.

sre-tl: jumping in. any chance this is the same kvcache eviction regression we saw last month?

dana: similar symptoms but logs point to API rate limit errors to cloud provider and ENI attach failures, plus packer sidecar OOMs. Could be a compounded issue. We'll check recent deploys.

jordan: deploys: no runtime changes in last 6 hours. However, a batch job from infra-team started at 13:55 that burst GPU allocation; correlated.

kevin: contacting infra to confirm if batch job can be throttled or shifted to other region. pinging @david-infra.

kevin: david-infra responded: will throttle batch job immediately and cancel non-urgent bursts. Should free up some GPU capacity in ~2 minutes.

sam: queue dropping rate improving. current queue 210 -> 160 in last 3m. Latency p95 still elevated but trending down.

maria: nice. suggest we keep manual nodegroup until autoscaler health is verified. Also run canary tests for autoscaler control plane: reconcile stress test.

jordan: capturing logs and uploading to incident artifacts. Link: https://artifacts.internal/PD-4521/trace.log

maria: next steps: 1) keep pager open until queue < 50 and p95 latency < 800ms for 10min 2) follow up with cloud quota team for GPU bump 3) postmortem owner: kevin 4) mitigation playbook updates to include immediate fallback cpu nodegroup option.

kevin: ack on postmortem. I'll start a doc and invite infra + platform.

sre-tl: once stable, re-enable autoscaler and monitor for steady-state. We should consider circuit-breaker in control plane to prevent rate limit storms.

maria: update at 14:12: queue 160, new nodes ready 6/12, sidecar restarts decreased. keeping pager.

pagerduty-bot: PD-4521: status=investigating, acknowledged_by=maria, escalated_to=sre-tl, linked_incidents=[]

sam: note - we observed a pattern: when packer sidecar OOMs, pods drop out of the pool, increasing queue and then autoscaler tries to react but hits provider limits. Might be worth adding proactive cache eviction policy to reduce memory pressure.

kevin: agreed. i'll add an item in postmortem to evaluate cache eviction TTLs and memory headroom.

maria: 14:18 update: queue 48, p95 latency 760ms. I'm going to un-ack only when stable. If no regression in 10m we can close the incident.

jordan: verifying all pods healthy across shards.

maria: PD-4521 will remain open until 14:28 unless regression. Great work team. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: PD-4521 status changed to monitoring (on-call).

maria: final note for thread: learned: autoscaler control plane should surface provider rate-limit errors as SLOs and trigger fallback sooner. Adding runbook note.

kevin: filing follow-ups. I'll take the postmortem.

sre-tl: thanks all, we'll convert to postmortem ticket and close PD once postmortem plan is in ticketing system.

maria: closing Slack thread updates. If anything pops, re-open PD and call page.
